segments.title: Gowind configurations from patrol vessels to light frigates
segments.body: The Gowind name covers vessels described as offshore patrol vessels, corvettes or light frigates, depending on configuration. The design question is how to fit the required capability into the smallest practical hull. At the lightly equipped end, some versions are characterized as little more than floating helicopter platforms. Others carry the equipment of fuller combatants. Shared hull shaping and bow lines connect the variants even as their dimensions and equipment change.

evidence.note: The Gowind programme spans OPV, corvette and light-frigate configurations.
The small-hull capability argument contrasts helicopter platforms with fuller warships and identifies shared hull shaping.

segments.summary: Gowind configurations range from offshore patrol vessels to light frigates, with a shared design approach that fits different levels of capability into small hulls.

segments.title: Gowind price examples and the currency caveat
segments.body: One price example is 80 million euros per vessel in 2014, adjusted roughly to 100 million euros for the time of the episode. The comparison then gives about 550 million per unit for the 2500 and 1.5 billion per unit for the 3100. A reference to Malaysian currency follows, alongside a statement that the comparison is being standardized on euros. Those larger figures therefore have an unclear currency basis and should not be read as settled, directly comparable euro prices. The intended point is the wide cost range within a family whose configurations differ substantially.

evidence.note: The price examples move from euros and an inflation estimate to 2500 and 3100 figures followed by an ambiguous Malaysian-currency qualification.

segments.summary: The price comparison illustrates how far Gowind variants differ, although the larger figures have an unclear currency basis.

segments.title: Gowind gun, missile and vertical-launch fits
segments.body: Weapon fits vary across the Gowind family. The Oto Melara 76 mm is presented as a common gun, with the larger 3100 versions instead carrying a BAE Bofors 57 mm weapon. Missile options include Exocet and Naval Strike Missile. At least two variants are described as having sixteen vertical-launch cells, while others have eight. Malaysia, the United Arab Emirates, Argentina and Egypt appear as examples of navies using the family to fill their requirements for hulls. These are differences between configurations, and the equipment list does not describe a universal fit for every Gowind.

evidence.note: Gun exceptions, anti-ship missile choices, eight- and sixteen-cell VLS fits and four customer navies are listed.

segments.summary: Compare the gun and missile options across Gowind variants, including Oto Melara 76 mm, Bofors 57 mm, Exocet, Naval Strike Missile and differing VLS capacities.

segments.title: Argentina's lightly armed Gowind patrol vessels
segments.body: The Argentine vessels are described as offshore patrol vessels of nearly 1,500 tons fully loaded. Their stated armament is a 30 mm gun and a .50-calibre machine gun. The same branch of the design can carry more equipment, but these ships have a maritime-security requirement. Their light armament matches duties with limited combat demands. They are assessed as among the most reliable ships in Argentine service.

evidence.note: The Argentine OPVs are assessed favorably for reliability, put at nearly 1,500 tons fully loaded, and linked to light armament and maritime-security duties.

segments.summary: Argentina's nearly 1,500-ton patrol vessels illustrate a Gowind configuration equipped for maritime security with a 30 mm gun and a .50-calibre machine gun.

segments.title: Warship status and authority in maritime security
segments.body: A naval vessel can be useful for maritime security even when its armament is modest. This role is easy to overlook in countries with large coast guards, where some encounters still call for the presence of a warship. The argument places weight on a warship's rights, duties, powers and responsibilities under international law. Its presence communicates that a nation state backs the force it carries. For encounters with fishing boats and other lower-level threats, that political authority can matter more than a large weapons fit. Unauthorized fishing by large fleets is the concrete example, because it can threaten the state's own fishery stocks.

evidence.note: Naval maritime-security roles in countries with large coast guards, warship status and state-backed force, with unauthorized fishing as the example.

segments.summary: A lightly armed warship can communicate state authority during maritime-security encounters, with unauthorized fishing as the example.

segments.title: Maritime protest, intent and the Greenpeace example
segments.body: In a personal criticism of Greenpeace and similar organizations, Alex Clarke treats attempts to stop other activities at sea as a maritime-security problem. He calls the tactics "protest terrorism" and suggests they could fall under terrorism laws at sea, without identifying a legal ruling. He attributes much of the damage to accidental mishandling of valves or controls, while also questioning activists' intentions and competence. These are his allegations and judgments about protest tactics, including a distinction between deliberate obstruction and the way damage occurs.

evidence.note: Personal accusations concerning Greenpeace and similar groups, including a terrorism label, asserted legal implications and judgments about intent, competence and accidental damage.

segments.summary: A criticism of Greenpeace's tactics distinguishes deliberate obstruction at sea from damage attributed to accidental mishandling, alongside personal judgments about intent and legality.

segments.title: Matching armament to piracy and disputed waters
segments.body: Some operators need Gowind variants for threats extending to piracy. An opponent capable of firing back creates a stronger firepower requirement than an encounter with a fishing vessel. State activity in exclusive economic zones, including disputed zones, adds another level of confrontation. Weapons then communicate willingness to fight as well as providing the means to do so. In that signaling role, a gun can have advantages over a missile.

evidence.note: The threat comparison moves through piracy and state disputes in EEZs to weapons as a signal of willingness to fight.

segments.summary: The threat changes the weapons requirement when patrol ships face armed pirates or another state's activity in disputed exclusive economic zones.

segments.title: Guns, warning shots and diplomatic signaling
segments.body: Missiles usually offer longer range and destructive capability, while a gun offers visible choices before a weapon is fired. Training it toward another vessel can communicate a demand to stop an unwanted activity. A warning shot provides a further step in the example of graduated pressure. A missile sitting in a vertical-launch cell or launcher offers little comparable indication through its direction, because the reorientation described here happens after launch. By that stage the weapon is already flying toward its target. Deliberately keeping guns trained away can carry the opposite message: the dispute remains serious, but the ship seeks talks without bloodshed. The advantage being argued is control over diplomatic signaling during a confrontation.

evidence.note: Gun direction, warning shots, missile launch and deliberate restraint are compared as ways to communicate intent.

segments.summary: A gun can signal intent through its direction or a warning shot, while keeping it trained away can communicate restraint during talks.

segments.title: Gowind's recognizable silhouette and naval presence
segments.body: Gowind's mast and overall shaping make the design visually distinctive. Another vessel can recognize the class as it approaches. That recognizability is treated as an advantage for naval diplomacy. The family's range of capabilities still depends on the size of the version selected and how much the customer is willing to spend.

evidence.note: Distinctive masts and shaping are linked to recognition and diplomacy before capability is tied again to size and cost.

segments.summary: Gowind's distinctive mast and hull shaping make it recognizable, adding a visual element to naval presence and diplomacy.

segments.title: Malaysia's Gowind choice and the FDI alternative
segments.body: Malaysia's selection is questioned against the possibility of choosing the French FDI frigate. The assessment favors FDI as a potential fit, while acknowledging that the alternative had a different procurement timetable. The Malaysian ship's laying down is placed in 2016, when FDI is described as still under discussion without an official contract. The FDI contract is tentatively recalled as following in 2017.

evidence.note: Malaysia's Gowind choice is compared with FDI, including a 2016 laying-down reference, tentative 2017 contract recollection and a preference for FDI's fit.

segments.summary: The Malaysian order prompts a comparison with FDI and an assessment that the alternative frigate could have suited Malaysia's requirements better.

segments.title: Available designs, operational needs and Malaysian delivery expectations
segments.body: An established programme offers the practical advantage of being ready to build when a navy places its order. That availability is the explanation offered for Malaysia's Gowind choice over the more conceptual alternative at the time. Operations must be carried out with the ships a navy actually has in service, so design preference alone cannot meet an immediate requirement. The resulting Malaysian vessels receive a favorable assessment of their capability. The closing delivery discussion gives an uncertain commissioning expectation of December 2026 or January 2027 for a Malaysian ship, alongside a statement that it was going for sea trials. Its full-load displacement is put at 3,150 tons. The commissioning estimate remains an expectation at the time of the episode.

evidence.note: The available-design argument is followed by a tentative December-or-January commissioning estimate, sea-trial reference and 3,150-ton full-load figure.

segments.summary: An available design can start construction sooner, but naval capability still depends on delivering ships into service. The Malaysian example ends with uncertain commissioning expectations.
